summary: Transient throughput degradation from scheduler 'slice shift' during peaky rebalance causing short-lived GPU shortages
description:
Issue summary:
During a short peak window on 2026-03-12 (11:03–11:12 UTC) NexaAnalytics observed periodic P95/P99 throughput regressions and request queueing on their dedicated pool. Root cause appears correlated with a scheduler 'slice shift' event: the scheduler rebalanced service slices across GPU hosts to accommodate ephemeral capacity signals, and during the handoff a set of short-lived allocation hold times caused transient GPU shortages for the customer's slices.

Impact:
- Customer-facing latency increased: p95 increased ~2.7x, p99 spiked up to 8s for batched routes.
- ~18% of requests experienced queuing / delayed start; no 5xx errors were reported.
- Affected a single dedicated cluster for NexaAnalytics in us-west-2; we estimate ~6 minutes of visible customer impact across repeated micro-windows.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: nexaanalytics-prod-dedicated-3
- Region: us-west-2
- Models: redwood-open-7b (primary), redwood-compat-3.5 (fallback)
- Autoscaling policy: predictive-autoscale-v2 with slice affinity and fast-burst disabled

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1. Scheduled a traffic ramp simulating a marketing burst to the customer's canary route (500 req/s sustained, mixture of short and long streams).
2. At ~11:03 UTC scheduler triggered a slice rebalance to reassign two large slices to new hosts (slice shift).
3. During handoff a set of prefetch/kv-cache leases were briefly invalidated and slot allocator held attachments for ~1.4–2.2s before rebind.
4. Customer requests routed to those slices experienced queueing until the new attachments were fully established.

Logs & traces (examples):
- scheduler: slice-rebalance: id=rb-20260312-1103, hosts:[gpu-51,gpu-78]
- allocator: hold-time: slice=nx-7b-3, hold_ms=[1400,2200,1600]
- serving-runtime: batch-start-delay: trace_id=tr-9a3f, delay_ms=1750
- monitoring: p99-latency spike event id=evt-20260312-1104

Why this is different from a typical noisy-tenant case:
- The symptoms are tightly coupled to scheduler timing: the rebalance introduced briefly elevated allocation hold times (not constant CPU/GPU noise).
- The event is repeatable in internal repro with simulated peaky slice shifts but does not match classic steady-state noisy-tenant behaviors (e.g., continuous kernel contention or memory thrash).

Investigation notes:
- Initial hypothesis: autoscaler mistakenly shrank then grew capacity causing placement churn.
- Telemetry shows autoscaler did not change target capacity during the window; instead the slice reassignment was initiated by the scheduler due to host health smoothing signals (short-lived thermal spike reported by host gpu-78).
- Host gpu-78 reported elevated thermal throttling from a background snapshotter job (not owned by NexaAnalytics). Snapshotter I/O increased NVMe latency which increased GPU handshake time and led to the slice being moved.
- Allocator metrics show hold-time distribution shifted from median 60ms to 1.4s for affected attachments.
- Repro script (internal): scripts/sre/repro/slice_shift_peaky_repro.sh reproduces the hold-time pattern locally when we inject NVMe latency via fio on candidate hosts.

Customer impact timeline:
- 11:02 UTC: pre-peak healthy (baseline p95 ~220ms)
- 11:03 UTC: marketing burst begins; scheduler triggers slice rebalances for hotspot mitigation
- 11:03–11:09 UTC: repeated short reassignments and two heavier handoffs; p99 spikes visible in SLO dashboard
- 11:12 UTC: traffic returns to baseline and metrics recover

Temporary mitigation applied (11:40 UTC):
- Disabled slice rebalances for the customer's pool for the next 24 hours (safety flag) to prevent further short-window churn while permanent fixes are evaluated.
- Provisioned an emergency small-burst reserved slot pool to absorb short-term peak fanout for NexaAnalytics.

Next steps (action items):
- SRE to add guardrail: when host health signal is thermal-only and short-lived (<60s), delay slice reassign by 30–60s to avoid handoff thrash. (owner: Marco Li, ETA: 2026-03-20)
- Infra to investigate background snapshotter cadence and throttle NVMe I/O to avoid GPU handshake impact (owner: Priya Natarajan, ETA: 2026-03-18)
- Product: review predictive-autoscale-v2 and scheduler interaction for slice affinity to reduce sensitivity to transient host signals (owner: Dustin Reyes, ETA: 2026-04-01)
- CS: customer-facing post-incident note and billing review for any overages during the incident window (owner: Alisha Kapoor, ETA: 2026-03-16)
investigation_notes: Telemetry correlation indicates root chain: background snapshotter I/O -> NVMe latency -> GPU handshake/hand-off delays -> scheduler slice reassign -> allocator hold-time spikes -> request queueing. Repro successful when NVMe latency injected. No evidence of model-level inefficiency or customer misconfiguration.
resolution: Workarounds applied: (1) temporary disable of slice rebalances for the customer's pool, (2) added emergency reserved burst slots. Permanent fixes: guardrail will be implemented to ignore sub-minute thermal signals for automatic reassign; infra will rate-limit snapshotter I/O and add NVMe latency alarms tied to scheduler-sensitivity thresholds. Customer notified and monitoring alerts added for quick detection. Close follow-up scheduled once guardrail PR merges.
